source.title: Implicature in Interaction: Understanding Implicature Improves Alignment in Human-LLM Interaction
source.authors: Asutosh Hota; Jussi P. P. Jokinen

record.tranche_reason: The study compares downstream implicature-interpretation performance across language models and reports that larger, more capable models align more closely with human interpretations. It uses a different task and measure from pretraining scaling-law studies and does not fit a scale-performance curve.
record.gate_note: Only Experiment 1's model-versus-human interpretation results bear on V6. Experiment 2 and Experiment 3 test prompted response evaluations and preferences, not whether downstream performance varies predictably with model scale. The authors' references to scaling laws are background, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: Experiment 1 compares five chat models from different families (GPT-4o, GPT-4, GPT-3.5, Llama-2-7b-chat, Mistral-7B-Instruct) on a 30-prompt implicature classification task. Parameter counts are stated only for the two 7B models. Scale is confounded with family, training and instruction tuning, and no scale variable, curve or pretraining loss is reported. The authors' claim that 'larger models align more closely' is qualitative and rests on undisclosed sizes. Their own numbers do not order by known scale: GPT-3.5 (33.3%) scores below both 7B models (50–53%). The study cannot show whether downstream performance improves predictably with scale, so it does not test V6. Kaplan et al. is cited only in the discussion ('scale alone is not the whole story'). The main contributions, implicature-aware prompting effects on user ratings and preferences, do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but incomplete. The paper's main conclusion is that implicature-aware prompting improves perceived relevance and quality (Exp. 2) and pairwise preference (67.6% on a post hoc selected set, Exp. 3). The authors also say larger models align more closely with human implicature interpretations, unevenly across classes. They add that scale alone may be insufficient, and that the results are not evidence of stable, human-like pragmatic reasoning.
record.recipe_differences: This study evaluates prompt-level implicature classification against human judgments; it does not measure held-out loss or fit scaling laws.
record.method_sensitivity: Model alignment varies by implicature class; the study reports especially weak Direction-seeking alignment for Llama 2 and Mistral 7B, and relatively strong Expressive alignment for Mistral 7B.

fits_no_version.finding: Across five chat models of different families, agreement with the modal human implicature label ranged from 86.7% (GPT-4o) to 33.3% (GPT-3.5). The two 7B open models (50–53%) beat GPT-3.5. Category-wise R2 is uneven, e.g. Mistral-7B Expressive 0.83.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pragmatic (implicature) classification ability differs strongly across chat model families. The differences are not explained by any stated scale variable.

record.code_released: Upon acceptance, the authors state they will release analysis code and materials; no URL is stated.
record.problems: The 30 prompts were authored using the same rubric being evaluated, so the authors characterize Experiment 1 as internal coherence rather than external validation. The model comparison is small and does not isolate model size from model family or other differences. No pretraining loss, parameter/token/compute sweep, scale curve, or extrapolation is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Experiment 2's prompting-condition effects on user ratings and Experiment 3's preference results are not extracted because they test prompted response evaluations, not downstream performance as a function of model scale or pretraining loss.
record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and the V6 supports/limits_scope labels are overturned. GPT model sizes are never stated, and family, tuning and recency are confounded with whatever size differences exist. The study's own ordering (GPT-3.5 < 7B models) undercuts a scale reading. The prompts were authored with the same rubric, so Experiment 1 tests internal coherence only.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy loss or sweep parameters, tokens, or compute.
The study does not fit small-run power laws or test predictions on larger runs.
The study does not compare compute budgets or test parameter/token allocations.
The study does not vary or compare architecture depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study tests neither other modalities nor repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling laws.

The study compares implicature task performance across a small set of different models, but does not measure pretraining loss, establish a quantitative scale-performance curve, or test prediction from scale.
The study does not examine scaling-law fit choices, exponents, compute-optimal splits, or curve bending.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Overall agreement with human labels on the authored 30-prompt implicature set
reader_labels.reason: The authors report higher overall agreement for GPT-4o and GPT-4 than for the lower-performing models, consistent with a qualitative model-capability trend (e1_agree_gpt4o, e1_agree_gpt4, e1_agree_mistral, e1_agree_llama, e1_agree_gpt35).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Category-wise alignment across information-seeking, direction-seeking, and expressive prompts
reader_labels.reason: Alignment varies substantially by model and category: GPT-3.5 and the 7B models have very low Direction-seeking correspondence, while Mistral 7B has high Expressive correspondence; this is not a uniform scale-performance pattern (e1_r2_gpt4o_info, e1_r2_gpt4o_direction, e1_r2_gpt4o_expressive, e1_r2_llama_info, e1_r2_llama_direction, e1_r2_llama_expressive, e1_r2_gpt4_info, e1_r2_gpt4_direction, e1_r2_gpt4_expressive, e1_r2_gpt35_info, e1_r2_gpt35_direction, e1_r2_gpt35_expressive, e1_r2_mistral_info, e1_r2_mistral_direction, e1_r2_mistral_expressive).
